---
title: "Using the Web Editor"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

`deck_serve()` starts a local FastAPI server backed by the same Python
engine `deck_build()`/`deck_validate()` already call, and opens a
React/Konva web editor against one project at a time -- the same
mental model as `shiny::runApp()`, not a hosted, multi-user app. Reach
for it when you want to see a slide's layout while nudging boxes
around, or when a teammate would rather drag an element than compute a
new `x`/`y` by hand; reach for `deck_get_config()`/`deck_set_config()`/
`deck_add_slide()` and friends (or hand-editing the YAML) when you
already know the exact value you want to write, since those are
scriptable and diff cleanly in version control the way a GUI session
never will.

## Starting the editor

```r
server <- deck_serve(project = "my-deck")
```

This launches the server in the background, waits for it to accept
connections, and opens its URL in the RStudio/Positron Viewer pane (or
your default browser outside an IDE). `deck_serve()` returns a
`deckifyr_server` object; keep it around so you can stop the server
later:

```r
deck_stop_server(server)
```

Unlike `shiny::runApp()`, `deck_serve()` doesn't hang your R session --
it's easy to lose track of the `server` object (a restarted session, an
overwritten variable). If that happens, stop it by port instead, no
object required:

```r
deck_stop_server(port = 8000)
```

This looks up whatever's actually listening on that port and confirms
it looks like a deckifyr server before touching it -- it will refuse,
with a clear error, rather than kill an unrelated process that happens
to occupy the same port.

Restarting on a port that's still held by an old deckifyr server (the
same situation `deck_stop_server(port = )` fixes) is common enough
that `deck_serve()` has its own shortcut -- `force = TRUE` kills the
existing server first, automatically, then launches as normal:

```r
server <- deck_serve(project = "my-deck", force = TRUE)
```

Same safety guarantee as `deck_stop_server(port = )`: it only ever
kills a process that looks like a deckifyr server, never just
whatever's occupying the port.

`deck_serve()` accepts `host`/`port` (default `127.0.0.1:8000`),
`presentation` (default `"presentation.yaml"`, relative to `project`),
`open_browser` (set `FALSE` to skip opening a window), `timeout` (how
long to wait for the server to become reachable), and `force` (above).
See `?deck_serve` for the full argument list.

The header always shows which project directory the running server is
bound to -- useful since `deck_serve()`/`deckifyr serve` only ever
serve one project per process, and it's easy to lose track of which
one after switching terminals or `deck_stop_server()`-ing a few:

## What the editor does today

Once open, the editor shows the current presentation's resolved slide
plan and lets you:

* Select a slide and see its elements laid out on a canvas sized to
  `design.yaml`'s own slide dimensions.
* Drag, resize, and rotate `text`, `markdown`, and `image` elements.
* Click a selected `text`/`markdown` element again to edit its text
  inline.
* Add a slide from the slide list's own "+ Add slide" button -- pick a
  named layout, or "Freeform (no layout)" for an empty starting point
  (`layout: null`), then give it an id:

  <div style="margin: 1rem 0;">
  <img src="../man/figures/web-app-add-slide.png" alt="The slide list's Add slide form open: a New slide id text field and a Layout dropdown listing the project's named layouts plus a Freeform (no layout) option, with Add and Cancel buttons below" width="700" loading="lazy">
  <p style="font-size:0.85em;">Adding a slide -- pick a layout or leave it freeform</p>
  </div>

  Each row's own corner carries two small icon buttons: a duplicate
  button (⧉, copies that slide's layout/elements/notes into a new
  `<id>-copy` slide right after it, no confirmation needed) and a remove
  button (×, a two-step inline confirm, not a browser dialog, with a
  reminder that Discard still undoes it right up until you Save).
* Toggle the slide list itself between **Slides** and **Layouts** --
  Layouts mode swaps the entire list to `layouts.yaml`'s own layouts;
  selecting one shows and lets you drag/resize/rotate its zones directly
  on the same canvas used for ordinary slide content. Unlike editing an
  individual slide, this toggle is a persistent, deck-wide mode: it
  stays put as you select different layouts (or the furniture
  pseudo-slide, still reachable above the list either way), rather than
  resetting per slide.

  <div style="margin: 1rem 0;">
  <img src="../man/figures/web-app-layout-tab.png" alt="The slide list toggled to Layouts mode: Slides/Layouts buttons with Layouts active, a plot-with-note layout selected, a banner reading Editing shared layout plot-with-note -- changes apply to every slide using it, the canvas showing that layout's two empty zone boxes, and an Elements sidebar listing its three zones (text: title, slot: figure, slot: note)" width="700" loading="lazy">
  <p style="font-size:0.85em;">Layouts mode, editing the "plot-with-note" layout's own zones</p>
  </div>

  The banner is a real warning, not decoration: a layout is shared, so
  repositioning a zone here moves it for *every* slide using it. "+ Add
  layout" (in place of "+ Add slide" while in this mode) creates a new,
  empty layout ready for zones; a layout's own remove button is a
  two-step confirm too, previewing which slides use it -- **except**
  the required `blank` layout, whose remove control is disabled outright
  (every project needs one to reassign slides to, spec's own fallback).
  Removing a layout that's still in use reassigns those slides to
  `blank`, but is rejected instead -- with a specific, actionable
  message, and nothing written -- if that reassignment would actually
  leave a slide unbuildable (e.g. an override that relies entirely on
  the removed layout's own zone for its `type`).
* Set the deck's own status (`metadata.status` -- "demo", "draft",
  "final", ...) and toggle the deck-wide status/watermark placement
  (`presentation.yaml`'s `status_indicator`) on or
  off, from a "Deck-wide" bar above the slide list -- without opening
  the config editor. Both are real, persisted edits: they write to
  `presentation.yaml` and change what the *built* deck looks like. A
  third, optional "Watermark override" field only matters when the
  mark itself should say something different from the deck status.
* Hide document furniture (background/watermark/branding/page number)
  from the canvas entirely with the toolbar's "Show furniture"
  checkbox -- **unchecked by default**. Unlike the toggle above, this
  is purely a local view setting; it never touches any file, and it
  exists specifically because a full-slide, on-top `watermark`
  placement otherwise sits right in the way of selecting and dragging
  the real content underneath it. Check it back on when you want to
  see where furniture actually lands:

  <div style="margin: 1rem 0;">
  <img src="../man/figures/web-app-furniture.png" alt="The same slide with Show furniture checked: the diagonal watermark and the branding/page-number corner placeholders are now visible on top of and around the real content, each labeled furniture: status / furniture: branding / furniture: page_number" width="700" loading="lazy">
  <p style="font-size:0.85em;">Same slide, "Show furniture" checked</p>
  </div>
* Add and remove elements from the right-hand **Elements** sidebar --
  one collapsed row per element on the selected slide (or layout);
  clicking a row (or the same element on the canvas) expands it into
  the same numeric box/rotation/z-index form dragging already updates.
  "+ Add element" opens a small form below the list: an id, an element
  type, and whichever fields that type actually needs -- a text area
  for `text`/`markdown`, a path field for `image`/`table`, a shape-kind
  dropdown for `shape`, nothing extra for `group`, and for
  `reportifyr`/`quarto` a dropdown of real candidate files already found
  in the project (reportifyr artifacts with a matching metadata sidecar;
  `.qmd` fragments), not a hand-typed path to get exactly right:

  <div style="margin: 1rem 0;">
  <img src="../man/figures/web-app-add-element.png" alt="The Elements sidebar's Add element form open on the title slide: a New element id field (callout), a Type dropdown (text), and a Value textarea containing sample text, with Add and Cancel buttons below the two existing markdown elements" width="700" loading="lazy">
  <p style="font-size:0.85em;">Adding a new text element from the Elements sidebar</p>
  </div>

  A new element gets a sensible centered default box, refined afterward
  by dragging/resizing like any other element; each row's own Remove
  button deletes it, no confirm step. `shape`/`group`/`table`/
  `reportifyr`/`quarto` elements can be added and removed this way, but
  still render as static, labeled placeholder boxes on the canvas -- see
  "Currently unsupported features" below.
* Select the synthetic **"⚙ Furniture"** entry above the numbered
  slide list to edit `design.yaml`'s `furniture` block itself --
  background/status-watermark/branding/page-number -- on its own
  canvas, with the same drag/resize/rotate interactions as ordinary
  slide content. The same Elements sidebar drives this: each furniture
  kind is its own row with Add/Remove buttons for materializing or
  clearing its style. Background has no draggable geometry of its own
  (it always fills the slide, so its row has a status hint instead of
  Add/Remove); the status placement can only be added once a placement
  is chosen in the "Deck-wide" bar above, and its "Hide" toggle only
  appears for the full-page watermark (the one placement large enough
  to bury everything else while you're positioning it).
* Edit `design.yaml`/`layouts.yaml`/`presentation.yaml` from the
  Config tab, either as a schema-driven form (the default view) or as
  syntax-highlighted, live-validated raw JSON -- toggle between the two
  at any time. Either way, nothing is written back to disk until it
  passes the same server-side schema validation `deck_set_config()`
  uses. Any field whose current value is a literal hex color -- most
  visibly `design.yaml`'s own `colors:` palette -- gets a small color
  swatch next to it, backed by the browser's native color picker:

  <div style="margin: 1rem 0;">
  <img src="../man/figures/web-app-color-swatch.png" alt="The Config tab's Form view on design.yaml's colors block: text, muted, primary, and accent entries, each with a small color swatch (black, gray, blue, red respectively) next to its hex value" width="700" loading="lazy">
  <p style="font-size:0.85em;">Color swatches on design.yaml's colors palette</p>
  </div>
* On the Build tab, see and edit where the built `.pptx` will go
  (`presentation.yaml`'s `build.output`) right there, instead of only
  through the Config tab -- either type a project-relative path
  directly, or click **Browse…** to navigate the project's real
  directory tree (one level at a time; a large, unrelated directory like
  a populated `renv/library` is never walked as a whole) and type a
  filename in whichever folder you land in. A **"Render slide previews
  (PNG + PDF) with this build"** checkbox controls `build.previews`: on,
  an ordinary Build also renders a PNG per slide and keeps the PDF
  LibreOffice produces along the way, right alongside the `.pptx`.
  Trigger a full build and watch it run as a background job, or trigger
  a **Preview** -- one, several (`e.g. 1,3`), or every slide. Preview
  needs LibreOffice; whether it's actually installed is checked up
  front, with an install link shown right there if it isn't, rather than
  only surfacing as a failed-job error after you click. Both Build and
  Preview show an animated progress bar while queued/running (the
  backend doesn't report a real percentage, so this is honest about that
  rather than faking one). A finished Build or Preview shows a thumbnail
  per rendered slide -- click one to expand it (only one expands at a
  time; click again, or click a different thumbnail, to collapse it) --
  plus a **"Show PDF preview"** disclosure, collapsed by default so a
  large PDF is never even fetched unless you actually ask for it:

  <div style="margin: 1rem 0;">
  <img src="../man/figures/web-app-build-preview.png" alt="The Build tab after a successful build with previews enabled: an editable Output path field with a Browse button, a checked 'Render slide previews' checkbox, manifest/pptx download links, five rendered slide thumbnails, and a collapsed 'Show PDF preview' disclosure below them" width="700" loading="lazy">
  <p style="font-size:0.85em;">A finished build with previews enabled: expandable per-slide thumbnails plus a collapsed PDF disclosure</p>
  </div>
* Download the resulting `.pptx`, its manifest, and any rendered
  previews once a build finishes.

## Currently unsupported features

Some things aren't supported by the editor yet -- worth knowing before
you reach for it instead of editing YAML directly. Each one links to
its tracking issue if it has one; if it doesn't, use the "open an
issue" link to request it.

* **No multi-select or clipboard.** One element at a time; no
  copy/paste, no group-move
  ([open an issue](https://github.com/jprybylski/deckifyr/issues/new)
  if you'd like this prioritized).
* **`shape`/`group`/`table`/`reportifyr`/`quarto` elements can be added
  and removed, but not dragged/resized on the canvas or have their
  content edited there.** They render as static, labeled placeholder
  boxes so you can see where they sit relative to everything else and
  add/remove them from the Elements sidebar, but repositioning by
  dragging or editing their actual content still means editing the YAML
  (or using `deck_set_config()`)
  ([open an issue](https://github.com/jprybylski/deckifyr/issues/new)
  if you'd like this prioritized).
* **`image` elements are draggable, but you won't see the actual
  picture.** The API that backs the canvas returns an image element's
  source path, not its pixels, so an image is a placeholder box too --
  one that participates in drag/resize/rotate like a real image would,
  just without a preview inside it
  ([open an issue](https://github.com/jprybylski/deckifyr/issues/new)
  if you'd like this prioritized).
* **No image cropping or snapping guides.** Positioning is freehand;
  there's no ruler/grid snap or alignment assist yet
  ([open an issue](https://github.com/jprybylski/deckifyr/issues/new)
  if you'd like this prioritized).
* **The furniture pseudo-slide only edits geometry (box/rotation),
  never the underlying text.** A status/watermark or page-number
  element's displayed word isn't a literal `design.yaml` field -- it's
  computed (from `metadata.status`/`watermark`, or a `{page}`/`{total}`
  format string) -- so double-clicking it there doesn't open a text
  editor the way branding's own literal `text` field does. Set the
  deck status from the "Deck-wide" bar instead, or the page-number
  format from the Config tab
  ([open an issue](https://github.com/jprybylski/deckifyr/issues/new)
  if you'd like this prioritized).
* **The schema-driven config form falls back to raw JSON for a few
  field shapes.** Most fields -- strings, numbers, booleans, enums,
  nested objects, open dictionaries like `colors`/`text_styles`, arrays
  -- get a typed input. A field whose schema allows more than one
  non-null shape (e.g. a `colors:` entry, which may be a literal hex
  string or a derived-color object) can't be disambiguated generically,
  so it's a small inline JSON field there instead of a fully-typed one
  (it still gets a color swatch when its current value happens to be a
  literal hex string, same as an ordinary color field). The Raw view (a
  toggle away) always covers the whole document either way. Comments
  and formatting in the on-disk YAML still aren't preserved through a
  save, in either view -- the same limitation
  `deck_set_config()`/`deck_*_slide()` already have
  ([open an issue](https://github.com/jprybylski/deckifyr/issues/new)
  if you'd like this prioritized).

None of this is hidden behind the scenes -- if you hit one of these
edges, dropping back to `deck_get_config()`/`deck_set_config()`/
`deck_*_slide()` or hand-editing the YAML files works exactly as
before; the editor and the CLI/R functions operate on the same files
and validate against the same schema.
